spec.title: Stub reachability, step 4: no stub a proof enters is left out of JBMC's gaps: the gap tests and the conformance corpus under JBMC and auto
spec.description: The JBMC gap preflight (lib/src/jbmc_gaps.rs) gained a third step: for the stubs its symbolic execution still enters, it runs the proof once more with a probe before each call site (a method of jvmcontract.StubProbe that fails an assertion behind CProver.nondetBoolean() and otherwise makes the call), and leaves a stub out of the gaps only when every probe and every unwinding assertion holds. This job guards that the step leaves out no stub a proof does enter. It runs, unchanged: the preflight's unit tests on the runner's JBMC (two of them run JBMC on lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-paths/P.java); the gap tests in lib/tests/integration.rs, which expect JBMC's stubs of a throwing JDK constructor, a JDK mutator, monitors and unlinked invokedynamic calls to be refused by name under strict, assumed under assume, and handed to contracts under advised and --confirm; and the conformance corpus under --engine jbmc and auto (the_corpus_agrees_with_the_jvm_under_jbmc_and_auto), where a stub wrongly left out would show as a JBMC verdict the JVM refutes. From llm-dlc/loops/stub-reachability.md, step 4.
spec.expected: every step exits 0: the jbmc_gaps unit tests pass, the eight gap tests pass with the gaps they name, and the corpus test passes (each JBMC and auto verdict agrees with the JVM)

resources.notes: the corpus under JBMC and auto took 1388 s at 1.6 GiB peak in 20261107-222356 (with the auto --confirm test too); the probe adds at most one JBMC run per proof whose symbolic run enters a stub; the gap tests take a few minutes; release build first
